title: DI Formula and Approach Tables
tagline: Year 4 — A one-page table of the formulas and approaches for tables, bar, line, pie and caselet data interpretation

introduction.overview: Data interpretation uses a small set of calculations again and again: percentage change, share of total, ratio, average, weighted average, CAGR, and the rule that a percentage must use the right base. This table pairs each calculation with its formula and the typical trap, and then gives an approach for each chart type: write the numbers, add derived columns, and use approximation when options are well separated.
introduction.placementRelevance: A quick DI sheet saves time because you stop deriving the same formula in each set.
introduction.realWorldContext: Business reporting uses the same small set of calculations.

learningObjectives: State the typical trap for each
Choose an approach for each chart type

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Percent change = change ÷ old. Share = part ÷ whole. Weighted average = total ÷ total weight.

coreDefinitions: Base: the quantity a percentage refers to.
Percentage point: difference between two percentages.
Derived column: a column you compute.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: Most DI is the same eight calculations in different clothing.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Write the numbers, name the calculation, check the base.

mainNarrative: Percent change from 100 to 125 is 25 ÷ 100 = 25%; the reverse change from 125 to 100 is 25 ÷ 125 = 20%.
A share rising from 30% to 35% is 5 percentage points, or about 16.7% in percentage terms.
A weighted average of marks 60 (30 students) and 40 (20 students) is (1,800 + 800) ÷ 50 = 52, not 50.
For each chart type: write the numbers in a table, add derived columns, answer from the table.

deepDiveAspects.title: Pie charts
deepDiveAspects.content: Shares must sum to 100%; angles are share × 3.6°.

deepDiveAspects.title: Line charts
deepDiveAspects.content: Read the slope: steeper means faster change.

solvedExamples.title: Percent change
solvedExamples.question: A value goes from 100 to 125. Percent increase? And the reverse change from 125 to 100?
solvedExamples.conceptOrFormula: Use the old value as base.

solvedExamples.title: Weighted average
solvedExamples.question: Marks 60 for 30 students and 40 for 20 students. Average?

solvedExamples.title: Points vs percent
solvedExamples.question: A share rises from 30% to 35%. Percentage points and percent change?

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Name the calculation, check the base, add derived columns, approximate when options are wide.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: Reject options that break a simple bound.

selfCheckQuestions: Can I tell points from percent?
